title: Abundant intelligence comes to Bangalore
text: The essay does not open with a thesis. It opens with one man's day.

title: Abundant intelligence comes to Bangalore
text: 5:56 a.m. Ravi wakes before his wife in a fifteenth-floor apartment in Bellandur. He is a graduate of IIT Madras, the son of a scooter mechanic from Hubballi who told him to work with his mind, not his hands. He stayed in India when classmates left for the West, and rose through a firm that does back-office accounting for American insurers.

title: Abundant intelligence comes to Bangalore
text: His work has ballooned. He now oversees delivery for five North American clients instead of one or two, but he no longer manages people. He checks the output of AI agents, built on Chinese models, and lately approves their reports without reading them. Graduate hiring has been paused for a year. Three of his team of fifteen have left, and none will be replaced. Margins are rising, and he is earning more than ever.

title: Abundant intelligence comes to Bangalore
text: 9:30 a.m. The local stock index opens at a record. On a call, the chief executive of the firm's American parent announces a restructuring: Ravi's division is cut in half, effective immediately, and staff across the subsidiary will fall by ninety percent over the coming months.

title: Abundant intelligence comes to Bangalore
text: 10:21 p.m. He gets home late. Riots have spread across Indian cities as layoffs mount, and youth unemployment in Bangalore has climbed from five percent to thirty. His daughter is studying with an AI tutor that costs almost nothing and is teaching her faster than her school did, toward what, he no longer knows. From the balcony, behind a new concrete wall and razor wire, Ravi and his wife watch smoke rise over the city and, for the first time in months, reach for each other's hands.

title: Abundant intelligence comes to Bangalore
text: Ravi returns in Part V, and his daughter closes the essay.

title: Intelligence is the giveaway. The conduit is the business.
text: Intelligence is the giveaway. The conduit is the business.

title: Intelligence is the giveaway. The conduit is the business.
text: Every great technology has paid its inventors less than it paid the people who controlled its distribution. Gutenberg went insolvent. The rail fortunes went to men who never built a locomotive. Manidis and Roberts argue that machine intelligence will follow the same path, faster. Frontier models are copied within months, so the price of any given capability collapses toward the cost of the computing power that runs it.

title: Intelligence is the giveaway. The conduit is the business.
text: The money, they argue, will settle in a few positions that intelligence has to pass through to reach the wider economy. Those positions are scarce, controllable and durable. Borrowing Lenin's phrase from 1922, the authors call them the Commanding Heights. The essay sets out six connected propositions.

title: Intelligence is the giveaway. The conduit is the business.
text: It is not only an investment thesis. It is also a warning. The same forces that create the Heights break the ladder of development for countries like India, close the door on emigration, and widen the gap between owners and everyone else. In the world the authors describe, there are only “sovereigns, exarchates, and the wretched.” The essay keeps both in view, and so should anyone reading it.

title: Intelligence is the giveaway. The conduit is the business.
text: 1Models commoditize.The price of a fixed level of capability has fallen about thirteenfold a year. Open models trail the frontier by roughly four months.Overture.

title: Intelligence is the giveaway. The conduit is the business.
text: 2The spending cannot stop.Training costs grow about 3.5 times a year. For one lab, falling behind means writing off everything already spent, so what is rational for each lab can destroy capital in aggregate.Part I.

title: Intelligence is the giveaway. The conduit is the business.
text: 3The state underwrites the Line.US growth, indexes and retirement savings now depend on AI, so Washington will backstop it. The true frontier moves behind government walls, and only America and China can stay in that race.Parts II to III.

title: Intelligence is the giveaway. The conduit is the business.
text: 4Diffusion runs on dollars.Cheap models reach billions of people through phones, paid in dollar stablecoins. That creates global demand for dollars and quietly exports US inflation.Part IV.

title: Intelligence is the giveaway. The conduit is the business.
text: 5The K widens everywhere.Offshore back offices are hit first. Licensed workers in rich countries are protected, and emigration routes close. Owners pull away from earners, and then from each other.Part V.

title: Intelligence is the giveaway. The conduit is the business.
text: 6Value pools at the Heights, which are not yet priced.Firms reorganize around a few operators paid like capital. Investors holding the last era's champions should rebuild their portfolios while the new positions can still be bought.Parts VI to VIII.

title: Costs rise, prices collapse
text: Each new frontier model costs several times more to train than the last. Meanwhile, competition and distillation push the price of last year's capability toward the cost of compute. The authors ask who could expect trillions in spending to be repaid in twenty-dollar subscriptions. Their answer is that durable margin will not come from the model layer.

title: Four curves that are really one
text: In the last quarter of 2025, investment in information-processing equipment added more than three times the growth of the entire US economy. Retirement accounts ride on the index, and the index rides on a few AI companies. That makes a stall politically intolerable. The authors expect Washington to sustain the Line with state equity in the labs and, eventually, by capping Treasury yields, as the Fed did from 1942 to 1951. As AI debt spreads, its correlation with the rest of the economy approaches one. Two bonds with the same rating may then fail together.

title: Four curves that are really one
text: The precedent is the Second World War. In 1942 the Federal Reserve fixed Treasury bill yields at ⅜% and capped long-term yields at 2½%, buying whatever investors wouldn't. The arrangement lasted until the Treasury to Fed Accord of 1951.

title: Four curves that are really one
text: The essay's reasoning: if the frontier becomes a matter of national defense, and the state ends up financing training costs that grow about 3.5 times a year, its borrowing needs will push yields up. Once those yields start constraining the program, the authors expect Washington to suppress them again, even if Congress has to change the Fed's mandate to do it.

title: Intelligence splits into three tiers
text: Why would China give its models away? Look at where each country keeps its savings. Chinese households hold their wealth in housing and bank deposits, so the party-state has little reason to defend high valuations for its labs. American retirements depend on the stock market, which now depends on AI labs. Cheap open models from China therefore hit the American financing model directly, and keeping the frontier funded may fall to the American state.

title: Intelligence splits into three tiers
text: The labs need things only a state can supply: permission to release their strongest models, predictable rules on foreign access, help with power and permits, financial certainty, and political legitimacy for gains that flow to few holders. A sovereign shareholder removes risks no private investor can.

title: Intelligence splits into three tiers
text: Tools short of seizure: a single “golden share” (as in the 2025 U.S. Steel deal), procurement contracts, cost-plus programs, and licenses for frontier training runs.

title: Intelligence splits into three tiers

title: America's strongest AI asset is its currency
text: The essay follows one payment. Malena, a freelance designer in Buenos Aires, triples her client list with an AI model. Clients pay her in a dollar stablecoin she keeps because the peso loses a third of its value each year. The issuer holds Treasuries, so she is helping fund US debt without ever having had a US bank account.

title: America's strongest AI asset is its currency
text: The second purpose of the Neo-Dollar is quieter. Beijing taxes savers by holding deposit rates down. Washington taxes them through inflation, and because the dollar is the world's money, part of that bill is paid abroad. A channel the economy must pass through earns revenue that rises with prices without needing matching investment. The authors see that as one more reason to own one.

title: America's strongest AI asset is its currency
text: A reserve currency lets its issuer debase and share the cost with everyone abroad who holds it. Billions of people already save in dollars out of preference and habit, and stablecoins extend that to people no American bank would serve.

title: America's strongest AI asset is its currency
text: The stablecoin itself pays its holder no interest. The income on its Treasury reserves goes to the issuer, at rates Washington sets. The essay sets this beside older, more visible takings: FDR's 1933 gold order, and the paydown of war debt at rates below inflation after 1945. The new version is quieter, and it reaches Buenos Aires as easily as Boston.

title: The first K split owners from earners. The second splits the owners.
text: Two months after the riots began, Ravi's keycard stops working. A machine-drafted letter tells him his job has moved to the “agentic services tier.” He gets six months' severance, and the parent company's stock opens higher in New York. The letter does not mention that his months of approving agent output were the training data for his replacement. His government offers him reskilling, perhaps in mechanical or farm work.

title: The first K split owners from earners. The second splits the owners.
text: For poor countries, emigration was the release valve for an educated surplus. In January 2026 the EU and India signed a mobility pact promising up to 100,000 multi-year work permits. The essay doubts it survives: Britain, France and Germany all hold general elections within three years, with anti-migration parties strong in each.

title: The first K split owners from earners. The second splits the owners.
text: The deeper reason is economic. As AI reduces demand for surplus labor, rich-country citizenship becomes more valuable and voters become less willing to share it. The authors note that an American passport already sells for $5 million and ask how generous anyone will be when it costs $50 million.

title: A Height is not a bottleneck
text: In 1922 Lenin let private trade back into Russia because the state still held “all the Commanding Heights.”

title: A Height is not a bottleneck
text: A bottleneck is a temporary shortage. A data center without a grid connection hands its margin to the power company until power is solved. Then the shortage moves to transmission, then to chips, and the margin moves with it. The authors call this endless cycle a “financialized Samsara.” A Height is different: it keeps a lasting share of the activity it enables, and that activity makes it stronger.

title: Management dissolves. Operators become capital.
text: The essay follows Guinness from a leased Dublin brewery in 1759 to a brand inside Diageo. Ronald Coase explained that firms exist because markets are costly to use. Intelligence lowers those costs and makes work legible, so labor leaves the firm. Offshoring was the rehearsal. What remains is a small group of operators, too valuable to pay as employees, who demand to be paid and governed like capital.

title: Buy DoubleClick and Android, not Alphabet or Anthropic
text: The essay's investment conclusion is blunt. The safe compounders in most portfolios are this era's newspapers. The fashionable AI basket is stuck in Genesis, mistaking itself for a Height. Meanwhile the ten-year Treasury yield, at 5.17%, has broken above its long-run average of about 4.5% since 1871. The authors read that as the end of a forty-year bond bull market, which means no more help from falling rates. Returns will have to come from owning the right positions.

title: Out from the garden, never to return
text: Out from the garden, never to return.

title: Out from the garden, never to return
text: The essay ends where it began, with a K that opens at every level. Ravi's daughter can reach the machine whenever she likes. She might reject it, or live the same life faster, or become something new. Perhaps the many in the middle will live long, content lives. The few who see and act, the authors write, will become a new shape of their own, and the rest of us their subjects.

title: Out from the garden, never to return
text: Then the frame widens. Technology has a direction, from cuneiform to the assembly line to the first atomic test in the New Mexico desert, and now to machine intelligence. They ask whether its makers felt what every parent knows: that the child may surpass them. We are heading, they write, toward a city at the edge of sight. They don't say when we will arrive, only that the road passes through older and harder human conditions before something entirely different.

title: Out from the garden, never to return
text: Their last instruction is to accept that the world as you knew it has already ended, and to prepare for what comes after.
